title: Fixed-object free-arrow pushouts compute variable-object attachments
statement:
Use small simplicial categories, the two-object categories $U(K)$ and the fixed-object categories $\mathrm{sCat}_O$ of [lem-coef-simplicial-interval-lifting], and the free-arrow functors of [lem-coef-fixed-object-free-arrow-adjunction]. Let $O$ be a small set, $a,b\in O$ (possibly equal), $i:K\to L$ any map of small simplicial sets, $C\in\mathrm{sCat}_O$, and $h:K\to C(a,b)$ a simplicial map. Let $\bar h:F^O_{a,b}(K)\to C$ be its adjunct and let $h_U:U(K)\to C$ send $0,1$ to $a,b$ with arrow map $h$. Form the pushout
$$P=C\amalg_{F^O_{a,b}(K)}F^O_{a,b}(L)$$
in $\mathrm{sCat}_O$. The canonical functor $U(L)\to F^O_{a,b}(L)\to P$, together with $C\to P$, exhibits $P$ as the pushout $C\amalg_{U(K)}U(L)$ in the category $\mathrm{sCat}$ allowing arbitrary object functions. In particular this variable-object pushout has object set canonically $O$. More precisely, for every small simplicial category $T$, restriction induces a bijection between functors $P\to T$ and pairs $(G,\ell)$ consisting of a simplicial functor $G:C\to T$ and a map $\ell:L\to T(Ga,Gb)$ satisfying $\ell i=G_{a,b}h$. This bijection commutes with postcomposition in $T$ and restricts to any prescribed object function $O\to\operatorname{Ob}T$. No injectivity condition on $i$, distinctness of $a,b$, or Kan condition is assumed.

source.place: Bergner, A model category structure on the category of simplicial categories, Lemma 3.4, horn case, printed p.11: comparison with the fixed-object pushout. Agent makes its implicit comparison precise for coincident attaching objects and arbitrary simplicial maps; no Stacks tag states this enriched pushout comparison.
